newsitem.title: HONG KONG: JAL to launch new domestic airline.
newsitem.headline: JAL to launch new domestic airline.

text.p: Japan Airlines (JAL) said a new subsidiary airline called JAL Express would be formally incorporated on April 1 with start up as soon as possible in the first half of fiscal year 1998.
The new airline is being set up initially with two Boeing 737-400 aircraft to operate regional domestic routes . Wholly owned by JAL, initial capital is 5.8 billion yen, a JAL statement said.

Industry observers said JAL Express is JAL's response to the threat of tough competition from "no frills" low cost and cut price airlines taking advantage of the Japanese government's new liberal aviation policy to challenge the flag carrier's traditional dominance of what has been up to now a highly protected market.

JAL Express has plans to expand to a fleet of 15 or 20 aircraft between 2005 and 2010, including larger Boeing 767 aircraft depending on route development. Cockpit crew will initially be non- Japanese but home-grown pilots will eventually make up the majority of crew. Cabin crew will be hired on short term contracts and also may perform ground duties, the JAL statement added.

The new airline will also operate some low demand flights for JAL under wet lease contracts as well as study the possibility of entering domestic trunk routes and short-haul international routes, JAL said.

Maintenance assistance for the new airline will be provided by JAL and Japan Transocean Air (JTA), which is based at Naha in Okinawa and in which JAL owns 51 percent. JAL Express will contract out airport handling, sales and management roles to create a "slim" structure, the statement added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
